beats.title: The Rigveda Is Composed
beats.description: Priests of the Indian subcontinent compose the first hymns of the oldest Hindu scripture, passed on by memory for centuries.
beats.note: Composition spans roughly 1500-1200 BCE; start year used.

beats.title: Mahavira Is Born
beats.description: A prince in eastern India is born who will renounce his wealth and become the final great teacher of the Jain tradition.
beats.note: Traditional Jain date; modern scholars place him later.

beats.title: The Buddha Is Born at Lumbini
beats.description: A prince of the Shakya clan is born in a garden in the Himalayan foothills, the future founder of Buddhism.
beats.note: Traditional date; scholars debate by up to a century.

beats.title: Confucius Is Born
beats.description: A teacher is born in the state of Lu whose ideas on virtue, ritual and family duty will shape East Asian life for millennia.

beats.title: Siddhartha Attains Enlightenment
beats.description: After long meditation beneath a fig tree at Bodh Gaya, a wandering ascetic awakens and becomes the Buddha.

beats.title: First Buddhist Council Meets
beats.description: Five hundred monks gather at Rajagriha soon after the Buddha's death to recite his teachings and monastic rules.
beats.note: Traditional date shortly after the Buddha's death.

beats.title: The Tao Te Ching Is Written
beats.description: A short book of eighty-one verses attributed to Laozi sets out the Way, the foundation text of Taoism.
beats.note: Approximate; scholars place it in the 4th century BCE.

beats.title: Ashoka Converts After Kalinga
beats.description: Horrified by the carnage of his conquest of Kalinga, an Indian emperor turns to Buddhism and non-violence.

beats.title: Buddhism Reaches Sri Lanka
beats.description: The monk Mahinda, sent by an Indian emperor, converts the island's king and plants Buddhism on Lanka.

beats.title: Han Court Adopts Confucian Scholars
beats.description: An emperor sets up official scholars of the Five Classics, making Confucian learning the core of state education.
beats.note: Traditional date of the Five Classics academicians.

beats.title: Buddhism Enters China
beats.description: Two monks arrive at the Han capital with scriptures on white horses, and a court sponsors China's first Buddhist temple.
beats.note: Traditional date; the story is legendary.

beats.title: Celestial Masters Are Founded
beats.description: After a vision of the deified Laozi, a Sichuan healer founds the first organised Taoist religious movement.

beats.title: Faxian Sets Out for India
beats.description: A Chinese monk walks across deserts and mountains to India to find Buddhist texts, then writes an account of his journey.

beats.title: Kumarajiva Arrives in Chang'an
beats.description: A scholar from Central Asia reaches the Chinese capital and leads a team that renders key Buddhist scriptures into fluent Chinese.

beats.title: Buddhism Reaches Japan
beats.description: A Korean kingdom sends a gilded Buddha image and scriptures to the Japanese court, starting a long dispute over the new faith.
beats.note: Traditional date from the Nihon Shoki; some sources say 538.

beats.title: Xuanzang Departs for India
beats.description: A Tang monk slips out of China to seek true Buddhist teachings, a seventeen-year trek that inspired a famous novel.

beats.title: The Kojiki Records Shinto Myths
beats.description: Japan's oldest surviving book sets down the creation myths and divine ancestry of the imperial line.

beats.title: Nara's Great Buddha Is Consecrated
beats.description: An enormous bronze Buddha is dedicated in a ceremony attended by thousands, a symbol of Buddhism's place in the Japanese state.

beats.title: Samye, Tibet's First Monastery
beats.description: A Tibetan king and an Indian master complete the first monastery in the land, rooting Buddhism in the Himalayas.
beats.note: Search confirmed: foundations laid c. 763-775, main shrine consecrated and first monks ordained 779; 779 used.

beats.title: Adi Shankara Is Born
beats.description: The philosopher who will revive Hindu thought through his teaching of non-dual Vedanta is born in Kerala.
beats.note: 788 is the most widely cited scholarly date; some scholars argue c. 700, and traditions give far earlier dates.

beats.title: Kukai Brings Shingon to Japan
beats.description: A monk returns from China with mantras, mandalas and ritual texts that become the Shingon school.
beats.note: Search confirmed he returned to Japan in 806.

beats.title: China Suppresses Buddhism
beats.description: An emperor orders thousands of monasteries closed and monks returned to lay life, a blow from which Chinese Buddhism recovered slowly.
beats.note: Great Anti-Buddhist Persecution of Emperor Wuzong, 845.

beats.title: Eisai Brings Zen to Japan
beats.description: A monk returns from study in China with the Rinzai meditation tradition and tea seeds.

beats.title: Nalanda University Is Sacked
beats.description: Invaders burn the great Buddhist monastic university of northern India, ending one of the ancient world's great centres of learning.
beats.note: Search: 1193 most commonly cited; Wikipedia and the site board say c. 1200, and the attribution to Khilji is disputed.

beats.title: Nichiren Declares His Teaching
beats.description: A Japanese monk chants a devotion to the Lotus Sutra for the first time and begins a new Buddhist movement.

beats.title: Kublai Khan Honours a Tibetan Lama
beats.description: A Mongol ruler names a Tibetan monk imperial preceptor, tying Tibetan Buddhism to Asia's greatest empire.

beats.title: Tsongkhapa Founds Ganden Monastery
beats.description: A reforming scholar establishes the monastery that anchors the Gelug school, later led by the Dalai Lamas.

beats.title: Guru Nanak Is Born
beats.description: The founder of Sikhism is born in the Punjab, the first of ten gurus.

beats.title: The Dalai Lama Title Is Created
beats.description: A Mongol ruler gives the abbot of a Tibetan monastery the title Dalai, meaning ocean, founding a famous line of leaders.

beats.title: The Guru Granth Sahib Is Compiled
beats.description: The fifth Sikh guru gathers hymns of the gurus and other saints into the scripture installed at Amritsar.

beats.title: Guru Gobind Singh Founds the Khalsa
beats.description: On a spring festival day, the tenth Sikh guru calls five volunteers forward and creates the order of initiated Sikhs.

beats.title: Brahmo Samaj Is Founded
beats.description: A Bengali reformer starts a society for worship of one God, rejecting idol worship and practices like widow burning.

beats.title: Shinto Split from Buddhism
beats.description: A new government orders gods and Buddhas split apart in shrines, elevating Shinto and sparking attacks on temples.

beats.title: Dayananda Founds the Arya Samaj
beats.description: A Hindu reformer in Bombay launches a movement urging a return to the Vedas and rejecting idols and caste by birth.

beats.title: Vivekananda Speaks in Chicago
beats.description: A young Hindu monk opens with the words Sisters and Brothers of America and introduces Hindu thought to the West.

beats.title: Cao Dai Is Founded in Vietnam
beats.description: A new religion blending Buddhism, Confucianism, Taoism and Catholicism is announced in southern Vietnam.

beats.title: Soka Gakkai Is Founded
beats.description: Two Japanese educators start a lay Buddhist movement based on Nichiren's teaching that grows into a vast organisation.

beats.title: Sixth Buddhist Council in Rangoon
beats.description: Monks from across the Theravada world gather for two years to recite and edit the Pali scriptures.

beats.title: Ambedkar Converts to Buddhism
beats.description: The architect of India's constitution and hundreds of thousands of followers leave Hinduism for Buddhism at a ceremony in Nagpur.

beats.title: The Dalai Lama Flees Tibet
beats.description: The Tibetan spiritual leader escapes over the Himalayas to India, where he sets up a government in exile.

beats.title: Hare Krishna Movement Founded
beats.description: An Indian swami opens a small storefront in New York and founds the society that brings chanting of Krishna's name to Western streets.

beats.title: Beatles Study Meditation in India
beats.description: The world's biggest band travels to an Indian ashram in Rishikesh to learn Transcendental Meditation from a guru.

beats.title: Dalai Lama Wins Nobel Peace Prize
beats.description: The exiled Tibetan Buddhist leader is honoured for his nonviolent approach to his people's struggle.

beats.title: The Bamiyan Buddhas Are Destroyed
beats.description: Two giant cliff-carved Buddha statues in Afghanistan are blown up by the ruling Taliban, despite worldwide protest.
